• Family: Amblycipitidae
  • Size: 7.5 cm
  • Temperature: 18-22°C
  • pH: 6.5-7.5
  • IUCN Red List: Not Evaluated
Asia: River Mengnai, Yunnan Province, China. Described from specimens collected from a tributary of the upper Irrawaddy in western Yunnan Province, China.
Inhabits streams with moderate to swift current, among stones and gravel.

Amblyceps yunnanensis, a new species (2016), was described from specimens collected from a tributary of the upper Irrawaddy in western Yunnan Province, China. It differs from all its congeners by the following combination of features: skin smooth with a complete lateral line; adipose fin originating at the vertical level of the anterior quarter of the anal-fin base, in the form of a low and smooth edge; dorsal fin with one very weak spine; pectoral fins without spines; caudal fin truncated without pinnate-like rays.

Etymology: the specific name yunnanensis uses the suffix -ensis, denoting place: western Yunnan Province, China, the type locality.

Froese, R. and D. Pauly. Editors. 2018. FishBase. World Wide Web electronic publication. www.fishbase.org, (10/2018).

Xiaoyan Zhang, Yan Long, Heng Xiao and Ziming Chen "First record of the catfish genus Amblyceps Blyth, 1858 from China with the description of a new species (Osteichthyes: Amblycipitidae)," Folia Zoologica 65(2), (1 July 2016).
